heard: Panic citizens in 1910 scrambled to buy gas masks and anti-comet pills. The bizarre panic began when astronomers detected toxic cyanogen gas in a comet's tail. Sensationalized media reports quickly convinced the public that this toxic gas would wipe out all life. The celestial culprit was Halley's comet, a famous visitor returning every 74 to 79 years. Even writer Mark Twain predicted his own death during this 1910 passage, passing away that April. But modern space probes revealed the terrifying toxic threat is actually a harmless, peanut-shaped ball of ice. Its giant 15-kilometer nucleus is blacker than coal, reflecting only about 4% of sunlight. This dark traveler safely returns around 2061, far too distant to make panicked citizens scramble.
